facts.summary: Utah: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due within 24 hours of separation.
facts.evidence_quote: (1)(a) When an employer separates an employee from the employer's payroll the unpaid wages of the employee become due immediately, and the employer shall pay the wages to the employee within 24 hours of the time of separation at the specified place of payment.
facts.source_title: Utah Code 34-28-5, Separation from payroll, resignation

facts.summary: Utah: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: (2) If an employee does not have a written contract for a definite period and resigns the employee's employment, the wages earned and unpaid ... become due and payable on the next regular payday.
facts.source_title: Utah Code 34-28-5, Separation from payroll, resignation

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Utah basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 The State law excludes from coverage any employment that is subject to the federal Fair Labor Standards Act.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Utah independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): No.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.value: Within 20 days of the new hire or rehire date.
facts.summary: Utah new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of the new hire or rehire date.
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of the new hire or rehire date.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Utah: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Semi-monthly (note 22); Monthly (note 22).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 22: Utah. Employees on a yearly salary can be paid on a monthly basis. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Utah is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Utah base new employer UI rate: Industry average (IndAvg).
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. IndAvg means the new employer rate is the industry average rate; get the exact rate from the state agency. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.

facts.summary: Utah experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.20% to 7.20%.

facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law.
